![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224622/assets/dadb1e7740ee89fbbf9cffe69501ebd7be655ec9aaee30071b09fc767e80092c.png)

Consider the finite region bounded by the curves $x=1+2y-{y}^{2}$ and $x=2y,$ as shown above. Find an integral expression for the volume generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
First, let $f(y)=1+2y-{y}^{2}$ and $g(y)=2y.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y) & =g(y) \\ 1+2y-{y}^{2} & =2y \\ 1-{y}^{2} & =0 \\ (1-y)(1+y) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solution corresponding to our region is $y=1.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=1.$ 

Now, let's draw our usual horizontal arrow through the region to determine the left and right functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224622/assets/d9f7cf87c59b7a0fc9600178795524f35a72b12466385e63eafa35c1fdb3537c.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the left function $x=g(y)=2y,$ and

- *leaves* through the right function $x=f(y)=1+2y-{y}^{2}.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}y([\text{right}]-[\text{left}])\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}y([1+2y-{y}^{2}]-[2y])\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}y(1+2y-{y}^{2}-2y)\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}y(1-{y}^{2})\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$
